q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of printing ink per kg?
title: Printing ink carbon footprint per kg
short: Weigh each raw material per kg of ink, such as pigments, resins, solvents, oils and additives, and multiply by supplier figures. Add mixing, milling and filling electricity divided by kg produced. Pigments and resins are usually most of the total.
audience: Ink makers for offset, flexo, gravure and screen printing

ul: Resins, varnishes and vegetable or mineral oils.
Solvents and additives, and the cans or drums.
High speed dispersers and bead or triple roll mills.
Solvent recovery, if fitted, and warehouse power.

p: Report per kg by ink type, since solvent-based, water-based and UV inks have very different recipes.

example.title: Worked example: ink plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 28,400 / 200,000 = 0.142 kg CO2 per kg
Add pigments, resins and solvents for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
